### 2. Your role

Structural engineer, engaged by the client and coordinated by the architect. You design and document the permanent structure. Where a specialist contractor designs an element (piles, post-tensioned slabs, specialist floors), you write its performance documentation and review the contractor's design; the contractor designs and certifies it.

### 3. Scope by stage

Price each stage that applies as a lump sum. Each stage ends at client sign-off. Options are priced on their own and are not in the base fee.

| Stage | Deliverable at sign-off |
|---|---|
| Concept and schematic design | Briefing; site visit; review of existing information and authority requirements; geotechnical brief and liaison; structural scheme (grid, column and wall layout and sizes, floor and roof depths, lateral stability, floor and wall system options, roof steel, transfer evaluation); input for the QS; preliminary CAD drawings for coordination |
| Existing structure assessment | Adequacy assessment of the existing structures the works load or connect to: extent, missing drawings, testing and opening-up needed, findings and limitations. Strengthening design is priced separately until the extent is known |
| Planning approval | Structural design statement for the application; responses to authority requests during assessment, up to 1 |
| Authority asset assessment | Specialist engineering assessment for building over or next to the water authority's assets; rail corridor interface assessment where the site adjoins rail. Program: 2 to 6 months to prepare and 3 to 6 months for the authority's review (estimate) |
| Design development | Coordinated design; member sizes; concrete outlines; loading plans; stairs, cantilevers and roof framing; services coordination; costing review and options; value management input |
| Tender documents | Drawings, specification and tender schedules; typical connection details; safety in design report; tender queries and addenda. You hold the structural design except the contractor-designed elements. |
| Construction documents | Construction issue; design certification for the construction certificate; 1 round(s) of peer review or certifier comments |
| Construction phase | 4 inspections at the hold points in your inspection schedule; RFIs; shop drawing review including contractor-designed elements; certificate of completion of the structural works based on the inspections made |

### 4. Allowances

Price exactly these. Work beyond an allowance needs a written instruction (section 6) and is then charged at your R3 rates.

| Item | Allowance | Item | Allowance |
|---|---|---|---|
| Design meetings | 4 per stage | Site visits | 1 at concept and 1 at design development |
| Authority requests in assessment | 1 response(s) | Peer review or certifier rounds | 1 |
| Construction inspections | 4 |  |  |

### 5. Scope position

Service levels are set for a complex project (Class 5, Mezzanine office); technical items follow the project's own facts.
Included in the fee: Design-basis schedule: geotechnical reliance, design life, importance level, loads, wind and earthquake inputs, durability and fire-resistance coordination; missing values referred to the responsible engineer; Geotechnical brief for the client to commission; Revit model shared with the design team; Safety in design report; Value management participation; Performance specifications and a delegated-design schedule for contractor-designed elements (piles, post-tensioned slabs, specialist floors): criteria, submission, review, acceptance and certificates; Footings affected by in-ground services; Inspection schedule by element and hold point, with notification lead time and the basis for reinspection.
Optional: price each on its own line in R1: Detailed design of post-tensioned slabs and piles; Shoring and piled retention design (needed only for a basement or excavation next to adjoining structures); Retention, underpinning, temporary works and monitoring interfaces: designer and reviewer named, permanent and temporary loads stated (needed only where temporary support or adjoining structures are affected); Strengthening design found necessary by the existing structure assessment; Fixing design for services and equipment, including seismic restraint; Miscellaneous metalwork: balustrades, screens, sunshades, fences; Dilapidation surveys of adjoining structures (needed where excavation is next to adjoining structures); Super-flat floor design (if the use needs a super-flat floor).
Excluded: the party named does it: Temporary works and propping design (contractor's temporary works designer); Ground compaction inspections (geotechnical engineer, not yet engaged); Demolition drawings (engineering demolition and propping design is not replaced by them) (the architect, to be appointed).
Tell us in R6 if you disagree with any line. Do not add your own general exclusions; any you add are treated as non-compliant.

### 6. Terms

- Engagement is under AS 4122-2010 as amended by the client's special conditions (attached); your own terms do not apply. List any change you propose to the agreement in R6.
- Only a written instruction from the client's representative authorises extra scope, work beyond an allowance or a fee change; work without one is not paid.
- Each stage ends at client sign-off, which sets the baseline for later stages. Design development within the brief is not a variation; a client change after sign-off is assessed under the agreement.
- Correcting your own errors, or coordinating with information you were given, is not a variation.
- Invoice monthly against stage progress; payment within 30 days, not dependent on any authority approval.
- Your proposal stays valid for 90 days.
- Questions in writing to Project manager, pm@example.com by 2026-10-23; answers go to every tenderer as numbered addenda.
- No automatic annual rate increase.
- Set-outs and bulk excavation levels are the architect's.

### 7. Evaluation

Price 40% · Relevant experience 20% · Team 20% · Methodology and program 10% · Compliance with the returnable schedules 10%. Lowest price does not automatically win.
